newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S. in deal for Canada to deport Saudi suspect.
newsitem.headline: U.S. in deal for Canada to deport Saudi suspect.

text.p: The United States has reached a deal for Canada to deport a Saudi man implicated in the 1996 truck bombing that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Saudi Arabia, the suspect's lawyer Michael Wildes said on Tuesday.
Wildes told Reuters the arrangement cleared the way for Hani Abdel-Rahim Hussein al-Sayegh to be deported to the United States from Canada shortly.
"I expect him on U.S. soil shortly. A deal has been cut," Wildes, a former federal prosecutor, said in a telephone interview from his office in New York.
"I believe that the arrangement serves both the interests of protecting my client's safety and the U.S. government's interest in investigating the Khobar Towers bombing," Wildes said in a statement.
Wildes said he would be appearing with Sayegh in Federal Court in Washington in the next few days.

The lawyer gave no details of the arrangement, but a source in Canada familiar with the deal said it involved Sayegh passing a lie detector test to say he was not involved in the Khobar Towers bombing in eastern Saudi Arabia last June. Sayegh would respond to questions about the Khobar Towers attack, the source said.
